subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add a native provider/auth quota-bucket contract for Gemini project/account quota failures, and should the first implementation live in core auth/failover or in the Google provider/plugin seam?
rationale: The decision sets public config/state shape, fallback defaults, provider ownership, status/probe output, and upgrade compatibility, which automation should not invent.

options.title: Add Generic Quota Buckets
options.body: Introduce additive bucket metadata and cooldown state while keeping today's flat key rotation as the default behavior.

options.title: Fold Into Pool Routing
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41135 explicitly own Gemini project/account quota buckets before implementing this slice.

options.title: Keep It Provider-Owned
options.body: Require the Google provider/plugin or external sidecars to manage project-aware suppression if maintainers decide core seams are already sufficient.

recommendation.title: Add Generic Quota Buckets
recommendation.body: Introduce additive bucket metadata and cooldown state while keeping today's flat key rotation as the default behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/config boundary decision over the auth/provider routing surface where steipete has the strongest feature-history signal.
